items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 120:1
items.html: Just as there are three aspects — conception, nursing, and Mochin — in all the Partzufim, so too there is the aspect of conception, nursing, and Mochin in their hairs as well. As the Rav explained in regard to the Mochin of ZA, that even its first aspect of conception does not come out except through the ascent of the Partzufim, when YESHSUT becomes one with Aba and Ima, and likewise Arich Anpin ascends and becomes one with Atik, as above, Page 914, Item 84; see there the whole continuation. And it is known that at the time of the ascent of the Partzufim the aspects of the garments of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK are nullified, and the statures of the coupling come out in the aspect of the revealed AB. Only afterward, when the Partzufim return to their place, they again clothe themselves in the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK, and the stature of the revealed AB again departs from them in the aspect of a returning surrounding light, and the reflected light of this departed revealed AB is the aspect of the hairs (see well above, Page 439, Item 6; and Page 443, Item 12). Thus even in the Mochin of conception there is also the aspect of the departure of the returning surrounding light and the aspect of hairs. And likewise in the Mochin of nursing and Gadlut. Now, the hairs of conception are called spikes, the hairs of nursing are called strands, and the hairs of Gadlut are called hairs, as written above in Answer 102, see there. (Page 363, Item 142).
